items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: whether you want to come from the technique of Charlie Parker or you want to use the technique of Lester Young or you want to use the techniques used by Ornette Coleman or John Coltrane or Sun Ra or somebody.

ctx.x: Because I think I’m fairly much chord oriented. I’m thinking about what chord I’m playing at the same time I’m thinking about trying to create a nice melody over the top of it. But if they’re not that familiar with chord structure yet, I’m not sure what to say to them.

Well you’re right, you have to have some understanding of harmonically what’s going on. But I will say you try to learn all of these various techniques and your phrases that you’re learning and themes, and then hopefully you can go on stage with the clean slate. And then you can just create based on what is provided to you by your musical environment at that particular time. So the pianist is feeding you something, the bass player is feeding you something, and the drummer is feeding you something, and I’m,…

learn from somebody how we do what we do. Nobody just took a baby and just left them there, they wouldn’t make it. You’ve got to have some kind of development, so you’ve got to at some point recognize the techniques and use some part of the technique whether you want to come from the technique of Charlie Parker or you want to use the technique of Lester Young or you want to use the techniques used by Ornette Coleman or John Coltrane or Sun Ra or somebody. But you’ve got to pull from somewhere.
